title: Landing-page or pitch test sized from the owner's baseline
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Whether a split test can answer the question at the owner's traffic and baseline, and what to do instead when it can't.
business_types: any with a website or sales calls
applies_when: A bold, diagnosed change is ready (BKP-04)
Owner asks for an A/B test
exclusions: Change is a minor tweak with no diagnosed problem
Test would need longer than the horizon (computed)
required_inputs: Baseline rate of the primary metric
A minimum change worth detecting (owner-confirmed or labelled heuristic)
evidence_requirements: Baseline rate of the candidate metric(s)
Reversibility and cost of the change
number of qualified first calls per week
call notes or recordings with consent
missing_data_behavior: Baseline unknown: fall back to the visitor floor and label it heuristic.
Too slow: pooled pages, an earlier metric, user tests, or a before/after read labelled observational.

decision_branches.if: Computed duration fits the horizon in whole weeks
decision_branches.then: Run the split with a numeric guardrail and a harm stop.

decision_branches.if: Too slow but change is cheap and reversible
decision_branches.then: Ship it with a pre-registered directional read (threshold set before data).

decision_branches.if: Founder-led pitch change at a few calls a week
decision_branches.then: No statistical test (about 173 calls per version at a 40% baseline and 15-point change); use the trusted-rep judgement test.

implementation_steps: Write the decision and minimum worthwhile effect
Run sampleSize for the outcome and for earlier steps
Pre-register metric, guardrails, end date and decision rule
Read with compareRates and sampleRatio; label strong vs directional
After each call: where lost, where excited, what was confusing
dependencies: Owner approval for any spend to buy traffic
K3/K4 storyboard turned into deck, demo, script

cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Event on primary metric and guardrails

metrics: Primary and guardrail rates per arm
Expected false wins = tests x alpha
leading: share of qualified calls progressing to next step
share of bad-fit leads exiting early
guardrails: Whole weeks, at least 7 days (existing lint).
An 85-90% threshold only pre-registered for cheap reversible changes and labelled directional (ExP rule otherwise).
No early stop on a win; harm stops allowed
No causal wording without a valid significant read
No close-rate 'win' claims without adequate sample (decisions.ts sampleSize)
alternatives_when_constrained: No tracking: user tests and owner tallies
No traffic: message lab in ads (experiment-design) only if budget is approved
No calls yet: test the insight and perfect-world criteria with 5 customer interviews (PB-interviews)
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
2-day tests (book's meek-tweaking example) miss weekday cycles
Rolling out to everyone at once

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: compute run time with sampleSize before recommending any page test; tweaks are never tested at small-business volume
proposed: when sampleSize weeks exceed 12 at the owner's call volume, present the pitch test as a qualitative pilot, not an A/B test

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: a lowered decision threshold must be set before launch, applies only to reversible low-cost changes, and the readout stays 'directional'

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: pooled multi-page tests report a per-page direction check before claiming a pooled effect
proposed: each pitch test logs per-call debrief answers and next-step outcome

unknown_to_investigate.rule: proposed: one horizon rule across skill and code (owner horizon, default 6 weeks) instead of 6 weeks in the skill and 12 in decisions.ts

reconciliation_note: Replaces PB-landing-split's fixed 700-visitors-a-week floor with a computed feasibility check (backlog CG-15).
